paragraphs.text: 送模型前自动给手机号/身份证等隐私打码、回来再还原的 DeepSeek Harness 插件
# dsh-privacy-shield
**In one sentence**: while you chat with the AI in DeepSeek Harness (DSH), this plugin swaps private
content in your messages (phone numbers, ID numbers, company names, addresses …) for untraceable pl
aceholders **on your own machine** before they are sent to the cloud model — then swaps them back so
you see the real values in the UI.
**v1.1.0** · MIT licensed · works out of the box · zero third-party dependencies
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A placeholder is a category label plus a random id derived with a key that never leaves your machine
— nobody can guess or enumerate the original value from it.
Your local chat history, the UI, and file exports **always keep the real values** — only the outboun
d copy is rewritten.
## What it does for you
- **Detects sensitive text automatically**: phone numbers, ID cards, bank cards, emails, license pla
tes, passports, plus Chinese-oriented types (organization and project names, system names, serial nu
mbers, addresses, person names) — 28 types in total. Everything is masked before it leaves your mach

ine; you don't have to do anything.
- **Understands tables**: when you paste spreadsheet-like conten
t, column headers decide which columns hold person names or organizations, and the whole column is m

asked. Amount columns are left alone by default so the AI can still do the math.
- **Understands JSO
N tool results**: what an agent prints after reading a spreadsheet — even a truncated, line-numbered
pretty-print dump that no longer parses as JSON — is still read column by column; key/value pairs (

`"sales": "…"`), aggregation maps (`{"paid_by_sales": {"…": 6}}`), and sheet names are masked too.
-
**Catches bare identifiers**: contract and project numbers like `cstb-pmc-2020245` or `京分-CSTM-PME(
PMC)-2020230` are recognised structurally, without a prefix or a cue word; plain dates stay untouche

d.
- **Remembers what it saw**: a value learned from a table cell or a key/value pair is masked wher
ever it turns up later in prose, even glued to Chinese text — with boundary checks so ordinary words

are not hit.
- **Learns your proper nouns**: scan local documents (`/shield scan-doc`) or learn fro
m chat history (`/shield learn`) to add your own people, projects, and systems to the vocabulary — c
andidates take effect only after you confirm them. Candidates come from multiple routes (column head
ers, same-sentence context, name suffixes, quoted titles, repetition), and each one shows the eviden

ce that nominated it; a name with no cue word in front of it still gets proposed.
- **Portable rules
**: export and import the vocabulary and switches as a pack (optional passphrase encryption). Handy

for a new machine or a colleague. A pack never contains the original-value mapping.
- **Double-check
s every request**: before each message is sent, the plugin re-scans the outbound text for anything t
hat leaked through unmasked. The audit log holds counts and type labels only — never the content its

elf.
- **Has a UI**: a status bar next to the input box opens a panel for settings, vocabulary, a ma
sking test bench, and audit records.
> **Two boundaries**: ① images are not inspected (no OCR) — please don't send sensitive images; ② ke
eping plaintext in local logs is by design — it's what makes restoration possible. Use disk encrypti
on and access control on your own machine.

ing once (output only, no side effects)

d doctor` | Self-check |

## How it differs from other masking plugins
1. **Only the outbound copy is rewritten** — local records stay original so you can always audit wha

t was masked.
2. **Placeholders are derived with a local key** — outsiders cannot enumerate or rever

se them.
3. **Rules packs never contain the restore table** — even a lost config file leaks nothing.
